title: sutra_read: suggest similar symbols on not-found errors
description: When sutra_read gets a symbol name that doesn't exist, it returns a bare 'not found: symbol X' error. Agents frequently guess plausible-but-wrong names (e.g. Db::save_snapshot instead of Db::insert_snapshot, SutraConfig instead of Config). Adding fuzzy/prefix suggestions in the error message would turn dead-end failures into redirects. Use the existing FTS5 or short_name index to find close matches and include top 3-5 in the error.
execution_record: Implemented as planned with two post-review fixes. Codex adversarial review caught: (1) unbounded CPU on long symbol inputs — fixed with 128-char cap + length-ratio prefilter before Levenshtein, (2) byte/char mismatch on Unicode — fixed with consistent char counts. The NotFound error Display was also changed to include next_action so suggestions are visible to MCP clients that only show the message field (not in original plan).

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review: needs-attention.

[high] Unbounded fuzzy scan — no length cap on symbol input; O(n*q*c) Levenshtein on every not-found.
[medium] Unicode byte/char mismatch — len() is byte-based but levenshtein counts chars; one-char non-ASCII slips past the <2 filter.

Fixes: cap query length, use char_count consistently for thresholds and normalization.
